title.analysis: Exact title: 7 Signs Someone is Wealthy (But Hides It). 41 characters. Numeral-led diagnostic list, third-person Someone, parenthetical reversal But Hides It; title case with lowercase is, no all-caps or year/urgency. Psychological proposition: privileged social decoding and reassurance that ordinary consumption can conceal success. Signs of hidden wealth is a plausible informational search query, but feed curiosity/status identity seems prominent; search volume and traffic unavailable. All seven signs delivered, but probabilistic title becomes categorical assertions in narration. No validated diagnostic accuracy or actual individual balance sheets provided.
title.script_alignment: Seven numbered signs delivered; reliability and universality unsupported

thumbnail.analysis: Inspected 1280x720 actual asset and 320x180 reduction: white background; large mildly smiling, half-lidded cartoon man in white polo/blue trousers left, hands in pockets; huge black HIDDEN / WEALTH / SIGNS right/top; curved black arrow targets grey older sedan with green glow lower middle. script.analysis: Coffee-shop stranger could buy building opens social mystery, Honda/BMW and whispers/screams contrast; creator authority and subscribe/like request precede first numbered payoff. Seven beats: 3E silence on earnings/expensive purchases/excess; older paid-off car and compound-return example; buying time via chef/private flights/cleaner; anonymity/security with unnamed wealthy anecdotes; value versus cheapness charger/roof; waiting/research/discounts; below-means home. Repeated transitions most revealing / completely rethink / might surprise renew anticipation but rarely add source evidence. Everyday scenes and moral contrast explain readily; no sourced household case or observation study. Final ties options/security to behaviors, then substantially repeats the same conclusion and Starbucks/Toyota/Ferrari callback, ending subscription and top1% next-video CTA. Potential engagement weakness is long preamble and duplicated payoff, not measured abandonment. Main shift: promises identify others, delivers aspirational personal habits. Strong value in differentiating consumption and assets; weakness is replacing visible-status stereotypes with reverse stereotypes.

claim_audit.claim: Most genuinely wealthy are masters of disguise; real money never needs validation; 3E most reliable indicator
claim_audit.assessment: Unsupported prevalence and diagnostic claims. No sampling frame, definition of wealthy, denominator, sensitivity/specificity or independent evidence. Modesty may reflect preference or low resources; conspicuous consumption may coexist with high net worth. Do not infer finances from privacy or vehicles. Creator years-of-study assertion and unnamed 50m/100m anecdotes are unverified authority, not population evidence.

claim_audit.claim: 600 monthly invested at 8% for 10 years exceeds100000
claim_audit.assessment: End-of-month deposits with nominal annual8%/12 produce109767.62, deposits72000; annual end-year7200 at effective8% produces104303.25. Both exceed100k conditionally. Not guaranteed, no tax/fees/inflation, uncertain market path. Nearby700/month then600/month changes illustration rather than an arithmetic contradiction. Car payment is not pure depreciation: includes principal/interest, and comparing requires residual value, purchase cost, repair/safety/insurance and necessary transport.

claim_audit.claim: Most cars lose majority value first5–7years; paid-off5–10year car wealthy norm
claim_audit.assessment: Direction of depreciation plausible but exact majority/age curve universalization not established here; model, condition, mileage and market vary. FTC used-car guidance supports history/inspection/recall and finance-cost checks, not a universal purchase-age optimum or rich-owner correlation.

claim_audit.claim: Time-saving services privately bought by wealthy, not normal people
claim_audit.assessment: 2017 PNAS research supports possible wellbeing benefits of buying time, not exclusive rich behavior or hidden wealth diagnosis; primary abstract explicitly says benefits not consistently limited to wealthy. Private chef and private aircraft are very different price tiers. Productivity benefit not automatically investment return; autonomy/care needs also matter.

claim_audit.claim: 20minutes researching15dollar charger but instant15000roof; always save time
claim_audit.assessment: Internal tension with blanket time optimization:20minutes worth more than maximum15dollar saving if valued above45/hour, before quality/safety/search enjoyment. Comparison itself not contradiction if genuine quality/urgency differs. Charger need/want depends on context; roof bids/inspection can matter even when urgent. No empirical wealthy behavioral rate supplied.

claim_audit.claim: Almost everything eventually on sale, most sales not sales; patience creates wealth
claim_audit.assessment: Unverified market-wide frequency; genuine discounts exist and waiting can incur costs. FTC deceptive pricing concerns do not establish majority prevalence. Correlation, reverse causality and constraints: existing wealth enables waiting, paying upfront and outsourcing. Habit imitation neither sufficient nor necessary for becoming wealthy.

claim_audit.claim: Everyone else mortgages40%income; rich housing modest
claim_audit.assessment: No population evidence for everyone else or income denominator (gross/net), monthly debt/housing definition. House size not total cost; location, tax, maintenance and income volatility matter. Living below means can preserve surplus but does not prove hidden wealth or guarantee returns. Privacy/security risks plausible, quantified risk reduction or true security from anonymity unverified.

ASR awkward fragments include genuine needs ones, they especially urgent and And I it's; preserved uncertain, no invented audio repairs. Ending recommends top1% video and stops after signs; no missing-script evidence, original audio not certified.

topic.analysis: Personal finance: stealth wealth, status consumption, frugality and financial autonomy. Evergreen social/status curiosity with accessible novice audience and everyday car/home/purchase examples. Main audience pain is comparison anxiety and desire to feel financially competent; no need for a particular market event. Avoid treating this as practical method to identify other people's balances. No historical Google Trends/keyword-volume evidence or publication-adjacent news demand established.
topic.novelty_and_corpus_angle: Seven-beat diagnostic wrapper mainly repackages familiar below-means/time-value advice. Owning ordinary car is compatible with many financial states. Distinctive 3E mnemonic and charger/roof contrast are memorable, not validated predictors.
topic.competition: Within-channel metadata shows secrecy/identity outcomes from WEAK to STRONG. Cross-channel matched source-level comparison not established for this unit; do not claim saturation census.

original_content_lesson.test: Test an original evidence-led consumption-versus-net-worth explainer with one concrete car-cost case and immediate self-check against generic seven-sign status spotting. Hold audience/topic/runtime reasonably matched; measure own appeal, retention and satisfaction separately. Falsified if concrete immediate self-check does not improve those outcomes or privacy/status version performs better. Do not infer causality from these competitor view ratios.
